_what: Load-bearing figures: numbers this site relies on across many articles. A figure used once is a local worked example and needs nothing. A figure carried by five or more articles is a claim about the world and needs a source and a date.
_deliberately_absent: Generic amounts that mean different things on different pages are registered only WITH a `context` list, never bare. The registry is keyed by the figure, so a bare entry for €2,000 as the Golden Visa state fee would hand provenance to every page using €2,000 as a price per square metre. That used to be a reason to leave such figures out entirely, which penalised sixty articles for using 10% correctly. Since the scorer gained context matching (`registeredHere` in scripts/lib/geo/score.mjs), an entry applies only where one of its context words appears within 140 characters of the figure, so the fee and the price-per-m2 are told apart. Bare entries still cover every use of their figure, which is correct for €800,000 and the other figures that mean exactly one thing here. Still absent and still editorial: €500, €800, €3,000, 2% and 8%, which carry no single sourceable meaning on this site.
_scope: 25 entries against 177 load-bearing figures. Coverage is deliberately partial and honest: entries are added when somebody has actually done the sourcing. The registry gate arms only at 80% coverage, so a partial registry costs nothing structurally and an invented one would cost the corpus its provenance credit entirely.

facts.statement: Minimum single-property investment for a Golden Visa in the prime zone: Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini and islands with a registered population above 3,100.
facts.source: Law 5100/2024, Article 5 (Government Gazette A' 46/2024)

facts.statement: Golden Visa threshold for the rest of Greece outside the prime zone, on a single property held under one title deed.
facts.source: Law 5100/2024, Article 5 (Government Gazette A' 46/2024)

facts.statement: Reduced Golden Visa threshold available where a building is converted from another use to residential, or a listed building is restored.
facts.source: Law 5100/2024, Article 5 (Government Gazette A' 46/2024)

facts.statement: Shortest lease a Golden Visa property may be let on; short-term tourist letting of the qualifying asset is prohibited for the life of the permit.
facts.source: Law 5100/2024, Article 5 (Government Gazette A' 46/2024)

facts.statement: Rate on the first band of annual rental income for individuals, applied to gross rent rather than to profit.
facts.source: Law 5246/2025, rental income scale effective 1 January 2026

facts.statement: Band inserted from 1 January 2026 covering rental income between €12,001 and €24,000; this income was previously taxed at 35%.
facts.source: Law 5246/2025, rental income scale effective 1 January 2026

facts.statement: Applies to rental income from €24,001 to €35,000 under the scale in force from 2026, having previously started at €12,001.
facts.source: Law 5246/2025, rental income scale effective 1 January 2026

facts.statement: Top rate on rental income, charged on everything above €35,000 a year for an individual landlord.
facts.source: Law 5246/2025, rental income scale effective 1 January 2026

facts.statement: Upper limit of the 15% rental income band; income above it enters the 25% band from 2026.
facts.source: Law 5246/2025, rental income scale effective 1 January 2026

facts.statement: Boundary between the 25% and 35% rental income bands under the 2026 scale.
facts.source: Law 5246/2025, rental income scale effective 1 January 2026

facts.statement: Threshold above which rental income is taxed at the top rate of 45% for an individual.
facts.source: Law 5246/2025, rental income scale effective 1 January 2026

facts.statement: Effective property transfer tax (ΦΜΑ) on a resale: 3% of the taxable value plus a municipal surcharge of 3% levied on the tax itself.
facts.source: Law 1587/1950 as amended, with the municipal surcharge under Law 1080/1980

facts.statement: Transfer tax due on a €400,000 taxable value, being the statutory 3.09% applied to the regional Golden Visa threshold.
facts.source: Derived: 3.09% ΦΜΑ applied to the Law 5100/2024 regional threshold

facts.statement: Transfer tax due on an €800,000 taxable value, being the statutory 3.09% applied to the prime-zone Golden Visa threshold.
facts.source: Derived: 3.09% ΦΜΑ applied to the Law 5100/2024 prime threshold

facts.statement: Standard Greek VAT rate, which applies to a first sale of a new build by a developer instead of transfer tax; the charge has been suspended on qualifying new residential deliveries.
facts.source: Greek VAT Code (Law 2859/2000) and the new-build VAT suspension

facts.statement: Annual flat tax on foreign-source income under the non-domiciled regime for a main applicant, paid regardless of the size of that income.
facts.source: Law 4172/2013 Article 5A, non-domiciled tax residents

facts.statement: Investment in Greek real estate, business or securities required to enter the Article 5A non-domiciled regime, to be completed within three years.
facts.source: Law 4172/2013 Article 5A, non-domiciled tax residents

facts.statement: Flat rate on worldwide income for a foreign pensioner transferring tax residence to Greece, available for fifteen years.
facts.source: Law 4172/2013 Article 5B, foreign pensioners regime

facts.statement: Flat deduction for repairs and maintenance set against gross rent; it is the only deduction an individual landlord may take under the standard regime.
facts.source: Law 4172/2013 Article 39, income from immovable property

facts.statement: Maximum stay in the Schengen area in any rolling 180-day period for a third-country national without a residence permit.
facts.source: Regulation (EU) 2016/399, Schengen Borders Code Article 6

facts.statement: Year-on-year increase in new Greek Golden Visa permits approved in 2025, against a backlog still in process.
facts.source: Ministry of Migration and Asylum, residence permit statistics 2025

facts.statement: Fall in foreign direct investment into Greek real estate in 2025 against the prior period, as buyers absorbed the higher Golden Visa thresholds.
facts.source: Bank of Greece, direct investment in real estate by non-residents

facts.statement: Share of international buyers in Greece targeting resale rather than new-build stock.
facts.source: RE/MAX Greece, 2025 international buyer data

facts.statement: Athens city-wide average gross rental yield, used on this site as a comparison baseline rather than as an achievable net return.
facts.source: Global Property Guide, Greece rental yields, November 2025

facts.statement: National average gross rental yield for Greece, against which regional and city figures on this site are set.
facts.source: Global Property Guide, Greece rental yields, November 2025

facts.statement: Golden Visa application fee payable to the Greek authorities by the main applicant. Adult family members pay €150 each and every residence card costs €16; minors are exempt from the application fee.
facts.source: Greek Ministry of Migration and Asylum residence permit fee schedule; Law 4251/2014 as amended

facts.statement: Golden Visa application fee per adult family member joining the main applicant's file. Separate from the €16 issued for each residence card.
facts.source: Greek Ministry of Migration and Asylum residence permit fee schedule; Law 4251/2014 as amended

facts.statement: Top of the all-in acquisition cost band on a Greek residential purchase, expressed as a percentage of the deed price. The band runs from about 7% and is composed of FMA transfer tax at 3.09%, notary at roughly 1.2% plus VAT, lawyer at about 1% plus VAT, land registry at 0.475% plus VAT, the engineer's certificate, and agent commission where one acts.
facts.source: Composite of Law 4646/2019 FMA transfer tax rate and the published Greek notarial, land registry and bar association fee scales
